besluite.rede: 'Bederfde kos' is ordinary, correct Afrikaans for spoiled food and matches the lesson's own 'bederf' stem in the heading and glossary, so 'bedorwe' is only a lateral move.
'Na daardie datum kan kos nog veilig wees' already reads clearly. Adding the article changes nothing a reader needs, so this is a lateral move.
'Daarop' covers the whole label, including allergen warnings printed outside the ingredient list, so narrowing it to 'die lys' moves the meaning of an allergy instruction.
The 'of' joins parts of one short sentence, so the AWS does not require a comma there, and the sentence reads well without one.

besluite.fout: 'n Lewende groeisel wat ook op kos groei' repeats the same stem and reads wooden.
besluite.rede: The repetition is a real fault, but this is a glossary definition, and 'voorkom' drops the idea that mould grows, which the next sentence builds on, so the writer should fix it.
''n Kos' (a dish or food product) is standard Afrikaans, and dropping the article in a glossary definition turns 'the ingredients of this food' into food in general.
